planning-learning-uuv.title: Unified Planning–Learning Framework for Robust UUV Navigation
planning-learning-uuv.authors: Md Ether Deowan and Eleni Kelasidi
planning-learning-uuv.summary: An observation-only navigation framework that couples persistent sonar mapping and clearance-aware planning with behavior-tree-guided reinforcement learning and latent predictive features.
overview: The system builds static and dynamic occupancy evidence solely from onboard observations, creates a clearance-constrained global route, and delegates short-horizon tracking and reactive avoidance to a learned local controller.

A behavior-tree teacher supplies structured supervision during PPO training. A latent world model encodes the observation history and exposes one-step prediction residual and uncertainty-proxy features, allowing guidance strength to respond to model uncertainty without claiming a calibrated collision probability.

stages.title: Perceive and map
stages.text: Fuse sonar observations into persistent static and dynamic occupancy representations.

stages.title: Plan globally
stages.text: Use clearance-aware Voronoi planning with event-triggered RRT fallback.

stages.title: Learn locally
stages.text: Train an observation-only PPO controller with staged behavior-tree distillation.

stages.title: Model uncertainty
stages.text: Use latent one-step prediction cues to scale supervision and inform the policy.

metrics.label: Task success
metrics.note: Curriculum-distilled PPO in the fixed multi-seed evaluation.

metrics.label: Collision rate
metrics.note: Compared with 40% for PPO without distillation.

metrics.label: Time-to-success
metrics.note: Versus 114.2 s for the non-distilled PPO baseline.

metrics.label: Practical-region success
metrics.note: Mean for S≤8, D≤9 and obstacle speed ≤1.5 m/s.

limitations: Results are simulation evidence, not proof of real-world readiness.
Dense scenes can exceed the nominal 50 Hz loop budget.
Transfer remains vulnerable to sonar artifacts, hydrodynamic mismatch, currents, pose drift and actuator delay.
Dynamic obstacles follow scripted motion and do not react to the UUV.

vision-uuv.kicker: Perception, localisation and control · Research preprint
vision-uuv.title: A Vision-based Control Framework for Real-time Autonomous UUV Operations
vision-uuv.authors: Erik Tjærand Frøland, Marco Job, Md Ether Deowan and Eleni Kelasidi
vision-uuv.summary: A modular onboard system for sparse and dense monocular depth, net-relative and global localisation, autonomous net following, and continuous volumetric mapping.

facts.label: Sensors
facts.value: Alphasense camera, DVL, IMU and pressure

overview: The ROS pipeline detects the repeating net-grid pattern with an FFT-based method, converts sparse geometric measurements into dense metric depth through TRUDepth, estimates net-relative pose, fuses vision with DVL and pressure for global pose, and updates a Wavemap occupancy representation.

The same estimates close the autonomous net-following loop. Experiments evaluated fixed-distance tracking, lawnmower patterns and an extreme low-light condition with all external pool lights off and onboard illumination at 25%.

stages.title: Sparse visual geometry
stages.text: FFT-based grid extraction estimates 3D net points from known mesh dimensions.

stages.title: Dense depth
stages.text: Vectorized TRUDepth completes sparse measurements into metric depth maps.

stages.title: Localise and map
stages.text: Relative pose, DVL-integrated global pose and timestamp-aligned Wavemap updates run onboard.

stages.title: Close the loop
stages.text: Guidance and PID control follow desired net distance, heading and motion patterns.

metrics.label: FFT perception
metrics.note: 47.8 ms mean processing time on Jetson AGX Orin.

limitations: Global pose assumes known net-pen geometry and negligible curvature in the flat-net experiment.
Performance degrades when little of the net pattern is visible.
TRUDepth can include background structures and slightly overestimate distance.
Fully vision-based velocity control remains open-loop and more disturbance-sensitive without DVL velocity.

mapless-uuv.title: Advancing Map-less Underwater Navigation
mapless-uuv.authors: Md Ether Deowan, Md Shamin Yeasher Yousha, Tihan Mahmud Hossain, Shahriar Hassan and Ricard Marxer
mapless-uuv.summary: A comparative study of PPO, TRPO, A2C, SAC and TD3 for 3D map-less navigation using multimodal sensing, monocular depth and domain randomization.

facts.label: Sensors
facts.value: Sonar, RGB depth cues and robot state

overview: Separate agents were trained across five waypoint environments and evaluated in visually distinct scenes with varied materials, textures, lighting and shaders. The study isolates algorithm, sensor-fusion and depth-prediction choices.
Depth Anything produced more stable training than MiDaS. Echo-sounder ablation exposed the importance of reliable geometric range, while domain randomization improved visual generalization.

stages.title: Encode observations
stages.text: Combine robot state, historical actions, range sensing and learned monocular depth.

stages.title: Compare learners
stages.text: Evaluate PPO, TRPO, A2C, SAC and TD3 under matched waypoint tasks.

stages.title: Randomize domains
stages.text: Vary visual materials, lighting, textures and shaders across training and evaluation.

stages.title: Test ablations
stages.text: Remove echo-sounder information and compare depth models to expose dependencies.

metrics.label: Best success ratio
metrics.note: TRPO with sensor fusion and Depth Anything.

metrics.label: PPO success ratio
metrics.note: With sensor fusion and Depth Anything.

limitations: Evaluation is simulation-based and uses separately trained agents for waypoint scenarios.
Depth Anything adds computational cost and parameter count.
Several SAC, TD3 and A2C conditions did not converge under the reported tuning.
Removing echo-sounder input increased conservative or risky decisions and travel time.

ur5-manipulation.title: UR5 Robot Control and Object Manipulation
ur5-manipulation.summary: A ROS 2 manipulation pipeline combining YOLOv8 object detection, RGB-D position estimation, inverse kinematics, trajectory planning, MoveIt 2 and a Robotiq 3-Finger Gripper.

facts.label: Task
facts.value: Detect, localise, approach and grasp objects

overview: The perception module trains a ten-class YOLOv8 detector and converts bounding-box centroids with depth into 3D target estimates. The manipulation stack then turns object targets into reachable poses, planned trajectories and gripper actions.
The work compares control interfaces and documents practical integration issues across perception, kinematics, MoveIt planning, servo-based adjustment, and Robotiq status feedback.

stages.title: Detect objects
stages.text: Train and deploy YOLOv8 as a real-time ROS 2 perception node.

stages.title: Estimate 3D position
stages.text: Combine image centroids with depth to obtain target coordinates.

stages.title: Plan motion
stages.text: Use inverse kinematics, trajectories and MoveIt 2 collision-aware planning.

stages.title: Execute grasp
stages.text: Coordinate arm motion with Robotiq gripper commands and state feedback.

metrics.label: Precision
metrics.note: Final validation precision reported for YOLOv8.

metrics.label: mAP@50
metrics.note: Detection mean average precision at IoU 0.50.

limitations: Similar green objects such as cucumber and leek were occasionally confused.
A few visually similar classes reduced stricter mAP performance.
3D position estimates were physically spot-checked but not evaluated with a formal metric protocol.
Further data augmentation, larger class-balanced datasets and grasp-logic refinement are needed.

turtlebot-maze.title: Autonomous TurtleBot3 Navigation in a Maze
turtlebot-maze.summary: A multi-robot Gazebo system for mapping, localization and autonomous maze navigation with synchronized behaviors triggered by external signals.
overview: The project builds a custom maze environment, generates a reusable 2D occupancy map, localizes the robot in RViz, and executes autonomous goals through the ROS 2 Navigation stack.
Its multi-robot layer coordinates behavior through external events, separating environment mapping, localization, planning and synchronized task execution.

stages.title: Build the world
stages.text: Create and validate the maze environment in Gazebo.

stages.title: Map the maze
stages.text: Use SLAM Toolbox to construct and save a 2D occupancy map.

stages.title: Localise and plan
stages.text: Visualize pose and goals in RViz and plan through Navigation 2.

stages.title: Coordinate robots
stages.text: Trigger synchronized behaviors through external signals.

limitations: Evidence currently demonstrates simulation behavior rather than physical deployment.
The available material does not include a quantitative navigation benchmark.
Performance depends on map quality, localization initialization and navigation-stack tuning.
